Swap pairs of columns in a data frame

Source: R/swap_cols.r
ks_swap_cols.Rd

Exchanges column contents by name: for each named argument lhs = rhs, the column named lhs receives the values that were in rhs, and rhs receives the values that were in lhs. Multiple independent pairs can be given in one call.

Usage

ks_swap_cols(df, ...)

Arguments

df

A data.frame, tibble, or other object inheriting from data.frame.

...

Named pairs col_a = col_b (bare names only). Each name that appears on the left or right must be a column of df, and each column may appear at most once across all pairs (no overlapping swaps).

Value

df with the specified column pairs exchanged (same class as the input where possible).

Details

The syntax USUBJID = SUBJID swaps the two columns: after the call, the column still named USUBJID holds the former SUBJID values and vice versa. This is useful when harmonising SDTM-style identifiers or fixing column order after merges.

With zero pairs in ..., df is returned unchanged.

See also

ks_aligndec

Examples

d <- data.frame(SUBJID = c("001", "002"), USUBJID = c("01-001", "01-002"))
ks_swap_cols(d, USUBJID = SUBJID)
#>   SUBJID USUBJID
#> 1 01-001     001
#> 2 01-002     002
